data.narrative:
Danti is a seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Jesse Kallman and Martice Nicks III that has raised $10.9M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector includes 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning similar maturity levels, though narrow peer-matching at the seed stage is constrained.

Of the three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($11M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding round yields an implied valuation of $27M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible; while 14 same-sector peers exist, none met the minimum threshold of three comparables within identical or adjacent stages and similar valuation tiers. Public-comp anchoring using the Space & Aerospace median P/S multiple of 27.4x could not be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue figures for the private target.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M to $31M, centered on $27M. This range reflects reliance on a single methodology and carries material uncertainty around (1) the appropriate step-up multiple for Danti's specific stage transition, (2) whether $11M raised is a reliable valuation proxy, and (3) the lack of revenue or comparable transaction data to cross-check the stage-progression result. A future funding round or revenue disclosure would materially improve valuation confidence.
